articles.title: Mariachi band's national anthem at Bears vs. Eagles game ignites racism debate and US Senator response
articles.summary: A mariachi band's national anthem before the Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles game ignited a heated social media debate and racism charges.
articles.body: To bring you up to speed, the Monday Night Football game between the Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles was preceded by the national anthem – performed by a mariachi band. And what has followed in the nearly 24 hours since that performance is a dispassionate, logical discussion about the quality of the performance and The Mariachi Herencia de México's choice of going for a big finish the crowd definitely didn't expect but mostly celebrated. Nope. Sorry, but social media doesn't do dispassionate or subtle music critique. CALEB WILLIAMS, LIMITED BY A HAMSTRING INJURY, SEEN CASUALLY PACING BEARS SIDELINE DURING NATIONAL ANTHEM What it has done is spawn an emotional and at times vitriolic debate that has included charges of racism by one of the group's performers, counter-charges of the NFL continuing an offensive outsourcing of America's game to foreigners ... ...And a United States senator getting involved. So, not tame stuff. And if you cannot abide the heated exchange, then stop right here because the next few paragraphs will get into it. But for the curious and engaged: SINGING THE CANADIAN NATIONAL ANTHEM AT THE BUFFALO BILLS HOME OPENER WAS A MISTAKE We begin with the performance itself. To an ear not trained in music's finer points, it sounded like any other national anthem early on in that the three-horn section of the ensemble led the way. Mariachi bands don't play salsa music, people. So no drum or bongo section setting the rhythm. Where it got a little different (sideways?) was when the ensemble, dressed in their full traditional mariachi garb including wide brimmed sombreros, seemingly tried for a big finish. And that big finish didn't sound like the traditional Star Spangled Banner at all. Well, it wasn't long before the critics hit the online streets. Some reactions: VICTOR WEMBANYAMA ANTHEM CONTROVERSY GROWS AS SPURS, NBA AND ESPN STAY SILENT DURING FINALS To be accurate, The Mariachi Herencia de Mexico is a two-time Grammy-nominated group out of Chicago. And they were brought to the game as part of the Bears' and NFL's celebration of Hispanic and Latin Heritage Month. The reaction to the group, meanwhile, came from both the left and the right sides of the political spectrum – with some people on the right questioning why the anthem was used to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month – even though Hispanics are the USA's largest minority group – and some people on the left basking in the fact the people on the right might be triggered. Some people from both sides also praised the performance. That wasn't enough for one of the group's leaders, Alonso Orozco Jr., who saw the negative reactions and charged they were racist. "Yesterday, we had the opportunity to perform the United States National Anthem for the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Eagles, and it was incredible to so so with love and respect for a great nation," Orozco posted on X. "However, a huge wave of racist criticism has emerged." What came next was a United States senator seeing an opportunity to dive into the fray that had nothing to do with United States Senate business. Arizona's Ruben Gallego came to the defense of the mariachi band. (And here I am, a United States sportswriter, writing mariachi band controversy play-by-play.) Anyway, here's the dispassionate analysis the online exchange missed: The NFL is indeed doing hard and consistent work to take America's game international. And while that will likely first include more games abroad and then teams in Europe, Mexico might decades from now also have a franchise. That NFL business decision has some fans in the United States upset because they see themselves as losing games when they're shipped abroad. That may explain some of the reaction that was then heaped on the mariachi band. But, to be fair, there were indeed some unkind comments online and none of those are apparent when other performers take unorthodox approaches to the national anthem, such as performing it with bagpipes. But, again, all of this happened online. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Nobody ran on the field playing a banjo to defend America's honor. One more thing: It is not racist to criticize a performance. It is not racist to have a dissenting opinion about the choice of performers or their performance. It's America, amigos. articles.title: Before Patrick Mahomes’ whopping $503 million deal, Brittany Mahomes shared his humble NFL beginnings at her father’s Texas home to save money
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes’ first NFL offseason looked nothing like his life after becoming Kansas City’s franchise quarterback.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes’ first NFL offseason looked nothing like his life after becoming Kansas City’s franchise quarterback. Following his 2017 rookie season, Patrick and Brittany Mahomes stayed in the upstairs guest bedroom at her father’s house because they wanted to save money while he adjusted to professional football. At the time, Mahomes had made one start and spent most of the season behind Alex Smith.That modest setup came before the MVP award, Super Bowl title and $503 million contract that changed the financial side of Mahomes’ career. His success also created opportunities outside football, and he has since invested in professional sports teams, restaurants, fitness technology, coffee and entertainment.Patrick Mahomes’ early NFL years began at Brittany’s father’s home before his $503M dealThe Chiefs selected Mahomes 10th overall in the 2017 NFL Draft, but head coach Andy Reid kept Smith as the starting quarterback. Mahomes appeared in one regular-season game before starting the December 31, 2017, finale against the Denver Broncos, when he completed 22 of 35 passes for 284 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City’s 27-24 win.Mahomes and Brittany then spent the following offseason at her father’s house in Texas, according to GQ’s July 14, 2020 profile of the quarterback. They used an upstairs guest bedroom to keep their living costs down, giving Mahomes a relatively ordinary start to his NFL career before Kansas City eventually handed him the starting role.The Chiefs traded Smith to Washington in January 2018, leaving Mahomes with the opportunity he had been waiting for, and he responded with 5,097 passing yards and 50 touchdowns during the 2018 regular season. He won the NFL MVP award and took Kansas City to the AFC Championship Game, establishing himself as the franchise’s long-term quarterback after just one full season as a starter.Mahomes followed that campaign by leading the Chiefs to their first Super Bowl victory in 50 years. On February 2, 2020, Kansas City defeated the San Francisco 49ers 31-20 in Super Bowl LIV after Mahomes helped erase a 20-10 fourth-quarter deficit, with the quarterback finishing the game with 286 passing yards, two touchdowns and the Super Bowl MVP award.Five months later, Kansas City gave Mahomes the financial security that had been impossible to imagine during his guest-room days. On July 6, 2020, the Chiefs agreed to a 10-year extension worth up to $503 million, including $450 million in new money and $477 million in guarantee mechanisms, keeping him under contract through the 2031 season.GQ’s July 14 profile showed another part of that transition when Mahomes discussed the Texas home he had purchased during the COVID-19 offseason. He told the magazine, “I have really nothing but a computer in here,” because he and Brittany had only recently moved into the property and were still setting it up.Mahomes also told GQ that he had become more selective with his time after finding himself overwhelmed by commercials, banquets and appearances during the offseason following his MVP campaign. That change gave him more room to think about opportunities away from football as his profile continued to grow.Patrick Mahomes turned his NFL platform into investments across sports, food and technologyMahomes began building a portfolio that went beyond traditional athlete endorsements, starting with professional sports ownership. He joined the Kansas City Royals ownership group in 2020 and invested in Sporting Kansas City in 2021, giving him stakes in two other major Kansas City sports franchises while he remained the Chiefs quarterback.Food became another area of interest when Mahomes invested in Whataburger as the restaurant chain expanded into Kansas and Missouri, while his investment in WHOOP gave him a position in a fitness technology company that closely connects with his own training and performance routine.WHOOP raised $575 million in March 2026 at a $10.1 billion valuation, according to reporting by the Times of India, although Mahomes’ private stake and personal return from the investment have not been publicly disclosed.Mahomes also moved into the coffee business when he became the lead investor and second-largest shareholder in Throne Sport Coffee in 2024, giving him an ownership position rather than simply serving as a paid celebrity endorser. His entertainment interests expanded through 2PM Productions, the production company he launched with his business partners to develop sports and entertainment projects.His investment portfolio reached another major sports league in October 2023, when Mahomes joined an investor group that acquired a stake in Alpine’s Formula 1 team. The group included several prominent athletes and formed part of a larger investment that valued the Alpine operation as a significant global sports property.Brittany’s own professional sports background has also become part of their business story without replacing Mahomes’ individual career. She played soccer at the University of Texas at Tyler and later played professionally in Iceland before moving into fitness, and she became part of the ownership group of the Kansas City Current. Patrick joined the NWSL club’s ownership group in 2023, while the team later opened CPKC Stadium in 2024.Mahomes’ NFL contract has continued to expand alongside those investments. On June 10, 2026, the Chiefs added two seasons to his agreement, taking the contract’s total value to $504.75 million, with incentives and escalators capable of pushing it to $522.25 million and a $64 million average annual value beginning in 2027.The financial picture now looks very different from the one Mahomes faced after his rookie season, when he and Brittany chose to stay at her father’s house rather than spend more money on their own place. That period came before the MVP season, the Super Bowl victory and the first $500 million-plus NFL contract, while the investments that followed have turned Mahomes’ football success into a broader portfolio spanning professional sports, consumer brands, technology and entertainment.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 0-17 watch for Dolphins: The case for and largely against a winless season in Miami
articles.summary: Miami looks as bad as it was feared before the season started. It has a roster that barely resembled an NFL team.
articles.body:
We all expected an exceptionally rough 2026 season for the Miami Dolphins . Their new regime includes a new head coach, new starting QB and new general manager. Pain was prevalent in the forecast, making this team a surefire target for smart survivor pool participants.

The Dolphins haven't proven those predictions wrong as they enter Week 4 with an 0-3 record and won't have their best offensive player, running back De'Von Achane, for the rest of the season. Preseason consensus set the Dolphins' win total at three or four. But was that number too high?

Yahoo Sports writers Frank Schwab , Eric Edholm , Jori Epstein and Jay Busbee each looked at how worried the Dolphins should be about flirting with the infamy of a winless season. Here are their answers to this question:

Is 0-17 really on the table for the Dolphins?

Frank Schwab: No matter how bad it looks now, it's still unlikely the Dolphins go 0-17. Give a professional team 14 more shots, even as a significant underdog, and it is likely to get a win.

But Miami looks as bad as it was feared before the season started. It had a roster that barely resembled an NFL team. The Dolphins are paying more in dead salary cap hits to players not on the roster than to players currently playing for them, which is a first in NFL history — and the roster got significantly worse without running back De'Von Achane going forward . Achane was the most talented player on the roster and now he's done for the season with a torn ACL.

The formula for a Dolphins win would be for QB Malik Willis to go off one week against a bad defense, but the best skill-position player around Willis is ... Malik Washington ? Or maybe Chris Bell, a third-round rookie less than a year removed from a torn ACL?

Make no mistake: This is the worst team in the NFL. But 0-17 is a difficult thing to pull off, so I'll say it's likely they avoid that history. But it might be close.

Eric Edholm: No team has gone 0-17 before, and there have only been two 0-16 seasons ever — the 2008 Lions and 2017 Browns. Somewhere along the way, somehow, the Dolphins will find a way to win a game.

No De'Von Achane is a cruel twist of fate, and this roster is extremely young. But we see fluky results every season — and nearly every week — in the NFL. The Raiders won in New England last season. The Panthers beat the Packers as 13.5-point dogs in Green Bay . The Vikings shocked the Lions that same weekend.

This was always going to be a long season in Miami, and the Dolphins haven't yet led a game in a meaningful way, but I think the coaching staff might be pretty good. It's going to take some time and some lumps, but I think there's an upset along the way.

They still have two games each against the Patriots and Jets , both 1-2, plus the winless Chargers still on the schedule. There are seven more home games. This is by no means a good Dolphins team, but I think it's far from the worst we've ever seen. So yes, 0-17 is on the table in the same way that "this plane could also land in the ocean" is on the table. The Achane injury made it more likely than it was before, but I still think we're taking about a one- or two-win team, not a historically inept one.

Jori Epstein: Only four out of 1,669 possible teams since the 1970 NFL merger have finished a regular season winless, per Pro Football Reference. So no, I'm not expecting the Dolphins to reflect .2% of history rather than the 99.8%. Even if we limit that sample size to teams who started the season 0-3, the odds of a winless season increase but still are highly unlikely: 98.6% of teams that started 0-3 went on to win a game.

Only four of 252 0-3 teams since the merger have finished winless: the 1976 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , 1982 Baltimore Colts , 2008 Detroit Lions and 2017 Cleveland Browns. Each time the NFL expands its regular-season slate, teams' chances to nab a win tick up.

For the tanking crowd: I don't recommend winless seasons. Developing rosters requires developing a winning culture. None of the four winless teams advanced to the playoffs in the two seasons that followed. The Colts took a full five more years to return to the playoffs. Landing a generational talent only to string together more losing seasons could wear down that generational talent before a turnaround takes place. So here's to the Dolphins eking out at least a win or two. And don't be surprised if they upset a playoff-bound team that underestimates them, like the Buffalo Bills or Denver Broncos . On any given Sunday ...

Jay Busbee: There's a famous line in poker that if you can't spot the mark in your first 30 minutes at the table, you're the mark. If you're Miami and you can't spot the guaranteed W looking at your schedule, well ... you're everybody else's guaranteed W.

Miami might not be favored in a game until the 2030s, but it's highly unlikely they'll go defeated the entire season. The talent margin between, say, the Bills and Dolphins is a lot narrower than even the teams in the Big Ten. Miami will catch fire for a game, catch someone napping, face a backup quarterback ... somewhere along the way, everything will break the Dolphins' way and get them a victory. Probably against the Bills because the NFL gods have a sense of humor that way.

That said, when getting a single freaking win is your stretch goal for the season, everything's off kilter. This ought to be a tear-it-down-to-the-studs offseason, and hopefully rebuilding with a good 2027 draft. Until then, Miami fans, practice a mindset of calm acceptance ... and enjoy warm weather all the way through the New Year, I guess.

articles.title: Ex-NFL Star Antonio Brown Set to Appear in Miami Court for Expected Plea Agreement
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown is scheduled to be in a Miami courtroom Wednesday to accept a plea deal will let him avoid prison time on a reduced charge in an attempted murder case, according to his attorney.
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown is scheduled to be in a Miami courtroom Wednesday to accept a plea deal will let him avoid prison time on a reduced charge in an attempted murder case , according to his attorney.

Defense attorney Mark Eiglarsh has said Brown will plead no contest to aggravated assault and be sentenced to probation. He also said adjudication will be withheld, meaning Brown will not be considered a convicted felon.

Brown could have faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original charge. Eiglarsh has said the agreement with prosecutors was too good to turn down. The Miami-Dade State Attorney's Office said previously that details would be clarified at the hearing.

Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a security staffer after a celebrity boxing match in Miami on May 16, 2025, and firing two shots at a man he was in a fistfight with earlier, according to an arrest warrant. Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told investigators that one of the bullets grazed his neck.

Brown has said on social media that he was defending himself from an attack and others were trying to steal jewelry from him.

Florida's Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Richard Cooper, an attorney for Nantambu, has called the plea deal a fair one. He has said Nantambu forgives Brown and would not cooperate with law enforcement.

Brown, 38, spent 12 years in the NFL and was an All-Pro wide receiver who last played in 2021 for Tampa Bay, including winning a Super Bowl with quarterback Tom Brady.

Over the course of his career, much of it spent with Pittsburgh, he had 928 receptions for more than 12,000 yards and accounted for 88 total touchdowns, including punt returns and one pass.

During a 2021 game with Tampa Bay against the New York Jets , Brown took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field, leading to his release by the Buccaneers and effectively ending his career.

Brown has dealt with several legal problems over the years. He previously was accused of battery of a moving truck driver , several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents.

Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai , where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June of the same year.

articles.title: Patriots rookie TE Eli Raridon announces death of newborn son after fatal birth defect diagnosis
articles.summary: Eli Raridon and his wife, Anna, announced that their son had been diagnosed with anencephaly.
articles.body:
New England Patriots rookie tight end Eli Raridon and his wife, Anna, announced the loss of their first child on Tuesday afternoon.

The couple shared a post on Instagram and announced that, after going in for a 20-week checkup, their son had been diagnosed with anencephaly. The fatal birth defect, according to the Cleveland Clinic , occurs when the fetal brain and skull doesn't develop as expected. This typically ends in a miscarriage.

"While we are absolutely devastated that we were unable to bring our baby boy home, I am grateful to have loved him deeply, kept him safe, and had been his home for the past 9 months before he was called back to Heaven," Anna wrote on Instagram. "I believe our little boy was lovingly knitted together in the womb by God, knowing how deeply he would be loved by our families, our friends, Eli, and me," she added later. "Though his time with us was brief, his life still precious, his purpose still meaningful, and he will forever be a part of our story."

articles.title: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak Has Strong Message on Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker III
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders defense will have its work cut out for it in Week 4 when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. Moreover, head coach Klint Kubiak will have...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders defense will have its work cut out for it in Week 4 when they face the Kansas City Chiefs . Moreover, head coach Klint Kubiak will have strong insight into one of the Chiefs' biggest weapons: Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III.

Kubiak was the Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator last season and was with Walker. The running back left Seattle in free agency this past offseason, signed with the Chiefs, and is off to an amazing start.

Through three games, Walker has played 151 total snaps, leading to a 90.6 overall PFF grade. Walker carried the ball 65 times for 360 rushing yards while averaging 5.5 yards per attempt on the ground and two touchdowns. He also forced 34 missed tackles and averaged 4.7 yards after contact per attempt.

Meanwhile, in the passing game, Walker has caught 11 passes on 15 targets for 82 receiving yards and two touchdowns. As a result, Kubiak knows more than anyone on the Raiders coaching staff how dangerous Walker can be and shared his thoughts on facing his former player.

"[Walker is] playing like one of the best backs in the NFL ," Kubiak said on the Sept. 29 edition of "1-on-1." "So, we have a big challenge. He's an elite talent. Love coaching him [and] he's one of the best backs in the NFL for a reason. He's making plays; he can catch the ball out of the backfield. He can do it all."

Raiders Will Need to Have Their Tackling Game on Point

Moreover, in that same interview, Kubiak noted that tackling is one of the fundamentals expected in this new culture he's building. However, tackling takes on even more importance in a week when facing a player like Walker, who can make a defense pay if it fails to tackle him, as Kubiak saw during his time in Seattle.

"That's just a pillar of our program," Kubiak added. "Those are things that you rep since April and things that have to be a part of your everyday drills. At the end of the day, football comes down to blocking and tackling. I would just credit Robbie and our defensive staff for the importance of fundamentals, but that's every week in the NFL."

Jon Gruden on Las Vegas ' 3-0 Start Ahead of Week 4

While the Chiefs have a standout offense heading to Las Vegas for Week 4, the Raiders offense is also riding an impressive form under Kirk Cousins . The veteran has a 67.5 overall PFF grade . The veteran also has a passer rating of 107.2, with 661 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, per StatMuse .

Furthermore, Cousins has recorded three big-time throws and three turnover-worthy plays. Amid this impressive start that not many saw coming, former Raiders head coach Jon Gruden shared his assessment of Las Vegas and why he doesn't rule them out as a Super Bowl contender.

"I think they're balanced," Gruden said on the Sept. 28 edition of "Wake Up Barstool." "They got a veteran quarterback. They got a great system of offense, and they got a fourth-quarter pass rush. I mean, they got guys that can heat you up at crunch time. And we got a good kicker so far. So, anything goes in the NFL.

"Anybody can win [the Super Bowl] thing right now. I don't see anybody that's truly dominant and unbeatable. But once you get momentum, momentum is a powerful thing and we'll find out about the Raiders this Sunday because the Chiefs are coming to town, and I can't wait to see that."

However, NFL writer Zach Jacobson pointed to both teams when discussing the decision. "This has just as much to do with Caleb Williams more than likely missing the game as it does with the Packers being flat-out bad," Jacobson wrote.

Analyst Michael Rodney joked about the move, saying he was "just happy the league didn't flex Packers/Bears to 5:25 a.m."

Patrick Finley also suggested that both factors likely played a role. "Guessing the Pack's struggles and Caleb Williams' uncertainty played a role in it," Finley wrote, while noting that the matchup "immediately becomes the best noon game."

Bears channel Just Another Year Chicago also highlighted Williams' injury and Green Bay's poor start as possible reasons for the move.

The earlier kickoff could also affect Bears fans attending the Chicago Marathon the same day.

The marathon takes place on Oct. 11, meaning some runners and spectators who expected the Bears-Packers game to begin later in the afternoon will now have less time between the event and kickoff.

Despite losing FOX's late-afternoon window, Bears-Packers remains one of the biggest games on the Week 5 schedule.

Chicago will head to Lambeau Field looking to build on its win over Philadelphia, while Green Bay will try to turn its season around after a disappointing opening three weeks.

articles.title: ‘Do We Not Acknowledge the Greatness of Ben Johnson?’ — Ex-NFL MVP Questions Why ‘Nobody’s Talking About’ Bears HC’s Masterclass vs. Eagles

articles.body:
The Chicago Bears beat the Philadelphia Eagles 27-7 on Monday Night Football with their third-string quarterback. Caleb Williams was out with a hamstring injury, and Case Keenum , making his first start since 2023, threw two touchdowns and added a rushing score as the Bears forced three Eagles turnovers.

It was a result very few saw coming. And for Cam Newton , the story was just as much about Ben Johnson as it was about Keenum.

Cam Newton Lavishes Praise On Ben Johnson's Tactics and Play Calling in Week 3 Win

Newton went in on the performance on his 4th & 1 with Cam Newton podcast, and his praise for the Bears head coach was hard to miss. Newton even mimicked Johnson's sideline demeanor in an exaggerated bit, smoking a cigar and holding a piece of paper to cover his mouth.

"Do we not acknowledge the greatness of Ben Johnson?" Newton said . "Listen to me when I tell you. I said to myself, Ben Johnson was in his… man, he was in his Goyard."

Newton noted the contrast between Johnson's composure and the sideline theatrics from Eagles counterpart Nick Sirianni.

"All you saw from Ben Johnson was him calling it. That's all he said all night. But he was in his bag, huh? He wasn't caring about all that stuff from Nick Sirianni. He was doing all that. I was reading the lips. I said, 'Boy, Nick Sirianni, boy, he got some…' Hey, man, he was talking to the referees, reckless, making threats across the field," Newton said.

He gave Keenum credit, too, but kept the focus on the scheme around him.

"Not to take anything away from Case Keenum, because he does deserve a lot of credit. But what is there to be said about the strong demonstration of the scheme, the preparation, and the play calling?" Newton said. "See why Case Keenum put on a master class for quarterback operations: identifying the Mike, minimizing any type of pre-snap insufficiencies and inabilities. The offense ran very smooth."

Through the early stretch of the 2026 season, the Chicago Bears are emerging as one of the NFL's most well-rounded teams. Chicago ranks eighth in PFN's NFL Offense Impact Score with a grade of 78.6 and ninth defensively with a grade of 78.8.

Newton also highlighted three things he felt the performance showed about Johnson's approach, which he described as the fundamentals that separate good teams from great ones.

"He did the dynamic three. Protected the football. Score when you have to. And then most of all, you got to bleed the clock," Newton said.

He pointed to fourth-quarter clock management as the key sequence of the game, arguing that such veteran tactics are increasingly uncommon.

"There was only one drive that he wishes he could have back. They went for it on fourth down. But they still played what they call the field position game. Those type of veteran tactics is what this game doesn't have a lot of," Newton said. "Protect your lead, protect the ball, you have to convert on third and fourth down, and then you got to bleed the clock, and you got to, most of all, finish the drive. Field goals is not finishing the drive."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Newton also pointed to the running game and how Johnson used it to keep Philadelphia's offense off the field. D'Andre Swift was quiet in the first half but contributed alongside the other backs in a way that served the game plan.

"He said, 'Listen, we got to run the football. We got to keep Jalen, DeVonta, them off the field on that sideline.' Yeah. Cause that last drive, y'all done flushed the toilet with eight minutes. Ain't nobody talking about that. We have to control the clock," Newton said.

Keenum finished with two touchdown passes, connecting with Luther Burden III for eight yards in the first quarter and Kalif Raymond for 41 yards in the third.

The Bears improved to 2-1 with the win. They will host the New York Jets on Sunday, Oct. 4, for their Week 4 matchup.

articles.title: Bills Announce Historic Josh Allen News Before Key Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is one of just four players in NFL history to record six or more rushing touchdowns in nine straight seasons. The post B...
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is off to a hot start that has put him in elite company in the NFL record books.

Allen has accounted for 11 total touchdowns through the first two weeks of the season, including six rushing touchdowns. The veteran quarterback's success on the ground has sent him to the top of the NFL and given him a rare place in NFL history.

As the Bills announced, Allen has now recorded six or more rushing touchdowns in each of the last nine seasons. There have only been three other players in NFL history to achieve that mark, all of them Hall of Famers — LaDainian Tomlinson, Marshall Faulk, and Jim Brown.

Allen is tied with Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry for most touchdowns this season, though Henry has needed 38 more carries to achieve his mark.

The Bills quarterback is coming off one of his worst regular-season performances in years, a three-turnover game against the Los Angeles Chargers . The Bills were able to overcome Allen's struggles — plus two more fumbles, one from James Cook and another from Dalton Kincaid — to beat the Chargers.

The Bills were able to storm back from a 10-0 deficit to go into halftime tied, with the defense surrendering just six more points en route to the 24-16 win. After the game, Allen gave credit to the defense for keeping them in the game.

"Sitting there to be tied at halftime felt like a dream, to be honest," Allen said . "Our defense played fantastic. It's not a game that you expect to win, but we'll take them any way we can get them."

The Bills have an early division test coming this week as they face a New England Patriots team that suffered a blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Bills would be able to jump out to a three-game lead with a win.

Though the NFL season is still early, Allen has already jumped to the top of the MVP race. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio noted that Allen's odds actually improved after Sunday's mistake-filled game, though he does face a strong challenge from another top quarterback.

"Allen has gone from +500 to +260 to win his second NFL MVP award. Behind him currently is 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy , at +425," Florio wrote.

"Purdy deserves to be high on the list. The 49ers are 3-0, and Purdy has an off-the-charts passer rating of 133.1. He has nine touchdown passes on only 83 attempts, with one interception. He's averaging 9.5 yards per attempt. Purdy also has 93 rushing yards and a touchdown."

articles.title: Week 4 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice for Fringe Flex Fantasy Football Starters
articles.summary: Surprises have been a big part of the 2026 fantasy football season thus far, and that trend certainly continued in Week 3.
articles.body:
Surprises have been a big part of the 2026 fantasy football season thus far, and that trend certainly continued in Week 3.

The week began with the Atlanta Falcons embarrassing the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau in Michal Penix's 2026 debut. That game featured massive performances by Bijan Robinson and Drake London. The week ended with the Chicago Bears rolling the Philadelphia Eagles behind the guidance of third-string quarterback Case Keenum.

We're sure to see some unexpected performances in Week 4. While it's hard to predict a breakout performance like Keenum's (247 yards, 2 TDs), we can dive into the latest results, examine the upcoming matchups, and make a few start/sit recommendations.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: Bucky Irving, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to overcome their 0-3 start without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield. Head coach Todd Bowles announced after Sunday's loss that Mayfield will miss at least three weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.

With Mayfield out, the Buccaneers will turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. In fantasy, that's likely to negatively impact pass-catchers like Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin. It could also hinder running back Bucky Irving, as opposing defenses are likely to force Daniels to beat them.

However, it's still worth trusting Irving in Week 3. He's been the clear lead back in Zac Robinson's offense, and Tampa is going to lean on him on both the running and passing games to support Daniels. He also has a favorable matchup against the visiting Packers this week.

Green Bay has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season. Robinson's big night last Thursday has a lot to do with that ranking, but Green Bay has been vulnerable up front all season.

Sit: Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Like the Buccaneers, the Los Angeles Chargers are still searching for their first win. They're also searching for some semblance of offensive cohesion under new coordinator Mike McDaniel. So far, the offense simply hasn't been very good.

The offense also hasn't featured a ton of Omarion Hampton in the passing game. He's only been targeted three times this season and has just two catches through three games. His lack of usage as a receiver limits his PPR floor significantly.

To come through in Week 4, Hampton may have to find the end zone, something he did in the first two weeks of the season. However, he was held to just 56 yards and no touchdowns last week and will face another stiff test on Sunday.

The Seattle Seahawks have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs and have yet to allow a rushing touchdown this season.

Start: Tetairoa McMillan, WR, Carolina Panthers

Tetairoa McMillan was the 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year, and the Carolina Panthers pass-catcher was off to another strong start in 2026. He tallied 10 catches for 176 yards in Carolina's first two games, but he was largely held in check by the Cleveland Browns in Week 3.

Though he was targeted five times, McMillan finished with just two catches for 17 yards. Cleveland used disguised coverages and a heavy focus on covering McMillan, and the Panthers struggled to adapt.

"That's something, as coaches, we got to look at and make sure we're putting him in better positions to be able to be effective for us," Panthers coach Dave Canales said, per Kassidy Hill of the team's official website.

Expect Carolina to adjust this week and for McMillan to have a bounce-back game against the visiting Detroit Lions. Detroit's defense has surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

While Keenum kept the Bears' offense rolling on Monday night, he couldn't turn Rome Odunze into the breakout star Chicago keeps waiting for him to be. The 2024 first-round pick has been a fine complementary receiver in his two-plus seasons, but he hasn't been a very dependable fantasy option.

Many managers hoped this would change following the offseason departure of D.J. Moore. It still might, but we haven't seen Odunze become an offensive focal point yet. He had five catches for 105 yards through his first two games and finished Week 3 with three catches and 44 yards.

Until further notice, Odunze should be viewed as a low-end flex option who will likely need touchdowns to shine. It's impossible to trust him against the New York Jets in Week 4.

The Jets have surrendered the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Justin Herbert's Struggles Analyzed by NFL Insider Amid Chargers' 0-3 Start to Season
articles.summary: Through three games, quarterback Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers offense has come nowhere close to meeting the preseason expectations that were heaped on the unit following the arrival of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.
articles.body:
Through three games, quarterback Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers offense has come nowhere close to meeting the preseason expectations that were heaped on the unit following the arrival of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

ESPN NFL insider Dan Graziano spoke this week to an anonymous NFL evaluator, who told him everything looks "difficult and exhausting" for Herbert amid the Chargers' 0-3 start.

Graziano added that he believes Herbert has appeared "confused and overwhelmed" by what he has been tasked with doing in McDaniel's offense.

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4

Herbert is completing just 59.1 percent of his passes for 627 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions, and the Chargers are already in dire straits as it relates to vying for a playoff spot.

They lost what were thought to be two highly winnable games against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders to start the season before going on the road and falling 24-16 to the Buffalo Bills in Week 3 despite the L.A. defense forcing five turnovers.

The Chargers only turned the ball over once, but it was a costly one, as Herbert was picked off on a third-and-5 deep in Buffalo territory while leading by three points in the fourth quarter.

Buffalo went ahead with a touchdown on the ensuing drive, giving the Bills a lead they would never relinquish.

Given what he accomplished early in his tenure as head coach of the Miami Dolphins, it was widely expected that McDaniel would work wonders as Herbert's OC.

The Dolphins ranked sixth in total offense and 11th in scoring in 2022, and first in total offense and second in scoring in 2023 with McDaniel at the helm.

Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had a career year under McDaniel in 2023 as well, leading the NFL with 4,624 passing yards and throwing a career-high 29 touchdown passes.

However, it should be noted that Tua had the benefit of electric athletes all around him, including wide receivers Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, and running back De'Von Achane.

Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Omarion Hampton have not come anywhere close to replicating what Hill, Waddle and Achane brought to the table, although Herbert hasn't held up his end of the bargain either.

There isn't much going right for the Bolts' offense right now, and things don't figure to get any easier, as matchups with the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens are on tap over the Chargers' next six games.
